To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
olive oil and omega- 3 polyunsaturated faty acids suppress intestinal polyps growth by modulating apoptotic process in APCMin/+ mice.
olive oil and omega- 3 fatty acids suppress polyp growth by reducing cell proliferation and increasing apoptosis.

dietary supplementation with olive oil and omega- 3 polyunsaturated fats reduces polyp number and size in ApcMin+ mice through an inhibition of fatty acids synthase and HmgCoA reductases and an increase of the ratio of ERβ to ERα.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diets rich in omega-3 poly-unsaturated fatty acids and olive oil on intestinal polyps development and progression in Apc(Min/+/+) mice.
the role of olive oil and omega-6/omega-3 polyunsaturate fatty acids ratio as modulators of the apoptotic process, which may be useful in the management and/or prevention of intestinal cancer.
the role of olive oil and omega-6/omega-3 polyunsat-urated fatty acids in the promotion and progression of colon carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
olive oil and omega- 3 polyunsaturated acids have the potential to prevent cancer development.

olive oil and omega- 3 polyunsaturated fats have a beneficial role in the prevention of intestinal polyps in ApcMin mice, which is mediated, at least partially, through the modulation of apoptosis and ERβ/ERalpha ratio.
a proper dietary intake of omega-3 fatty acids and olive oil may contribute to the prevention of colon cancer development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of dietary supplements containing omega-3 poly-unsaturated fatty acids and olive oil may have a beneficial effect in the prevention of colorectal cancer.
olive oil and salmon fish oil can reduce the number of polyps in mice that have a genetic defect in the APC gene.
a proper dietary intake of olive oil, fish, and fish oils could reduce cancer risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of a diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids and/or olive oil can be beneficial for the prevention of colorectal cancer.

a diet rich in natural compounds can modulate the expression of key enzymes involved in the synthesis of fatty acids and cholesterol, which in turn may influence the expression and function of ERs, and thus may be beneficial to prevent the onset and progression or even reverse the development of cancer.
a diet enriched with natural products, such as olive and fish oils, may be a useful strategy in the prevention and treatment of colon cancer.
